title: Low-Power Ultrasonic Communication Through Metallic Structures
content: Ultrasonic communication enables data to be transmitted through electrically conductive barriers where radio-frequency transmission is significantly attenuated. The energy consumption of the communication system is a primary design constraint for the integration into sensor nodes with limited energy resources. Therefore, this contribution presents a low-power, half-duplex ultrasonic transceiver for through-metal communication. Suitable modulation schemes are evaluated on the basis of the acoustic channel impulse response, and a differential phase-shift keying (DPSK) is implemented on an embedded platform. The system establishes a communication link with a data rate of 202 kbps at a carrier frequency of 1.2 MHz through a 1.6 mm thick metal barrier. The experimental results demonstrate an energy efficiency of 233 nJ/bit for the transmitter and 342 nJ/bit for the receiver with a bit error rate of 2.5×10−7.
